column11: none of it, and the trial excludes the approved population by name. VIJOICE 'is indicated for the treatment of adult and pediatric patients 2 years of age and older with severe manifestations of PIK3CA-Related Overgrowth Spectrum (PROS) who require systemic therapy' (DailyMed setid 638069a4-aee0-46c9-9e21-54ad449c163c, revised 7/2025); PIQRAY is indicated with fulvestrant in HR-positive, HER2-negative, PIK3CA-mutated advanced or metastatic breast cancer (DailyMed setid b20b4e18-7a4b-4500-a08f-06c6dab0ee5b, effective 2026-11-05). NCT05948943 requires that 'the physician must confirm that the LyM cannot be included under the PROS diagnostic criteria' and excludes any participant with 'a physician-confirmed and documented diagnosis of PROS at the time of informed consent'. The two populations are disjoint by the protocol's own construction
column12: the trial also excludes central conducting lymphatic anomaly, generalised lymphatic anomaly, Gorham-Stout disease and kaposiform lymphangiomatosis, none of which is in either label either, so the exclusions do not cut into the base

column11: Gallagher JR, Martini J, Carroll S, Small A, Teng J, 'Annual prevalence estimation of lymphatic malformation with a cutaneous component: observational study of a national representative sample of physicians', Orphanet J Rare Dis 2022;17(1):192 (doi 10.1186/s13023-022-02336-3, PMID 35550604, PMC9097327), a weighted survey of 316 US patient-care physicians in the specialties that manage the condition: 'Our survey results indicated the estimated number of unique annually managed LMC patients by target specialists is 79,920 (CI 66,600-93,250). This number corresponds to managed prevalence of 24.1 LMC patients per 100,000 population (CI 19.6/100,000-28.4/100,000).' The managed count is used rather than the rate so no second denominator enters
column12: a managed prevalence, which is the right basis for a prescribable pool and the wrong one for the disease: it counts only patients a specialist saw in the past 12 months. It is also narrower than the trial on one axis and wider on another. Narrower, because it counts lymphatic malformations with a cutaneous component, microcystic or mixed, and NCT05948943 admits any symptomatic lymphatic malformation including purely internal macrocystic disease. Wider, because it is a physician self-estimate survey rather than a registry or a claims count. The birth-cohort literature gives an incidence of 1 in 6,000 to 1 in 16,000 live births for lymphatic malformations as a whole (Radiologie (Heidelb) 2025;65(5):354-361, doi 10.1007/s00117-025-01450-0), which is a range and is not carried as a number

column11: stated at nil, the convention the book already uses on 38 rows where a prevalent pool has no usable US inflow. A lymphatic malformation is congenital and lifelong, the source above is a count of patients under management rather than a flow into care, and the published birth incidence is a range (1 in 6,000 to 1 in 16,000 live births) rather than a figure. forecast.pool_rule reads a nil inflow as a closed pool
column12: nil is a modelling statement, not a claim that no child is born with the disease. It makes the untreated pool carry over in full, which is generous to cumulative uptake

column11: the PIK3CA-mutant share, which NCT05948943 requires: 'Participant has evidence of a somatic mutation(s) in the PIK3CA gene prior to randomization.' Brouillard P, Schlogel MJ, Homayun Sepehr N et al., 'Non-hotspot PIK3CA mutations are more frequent in CLOVES than in common or combined lymphatic malformations', Orphanet J Rare Dis 2021;16(1):267 (doi 10.1186/s13023-021-01898-y, PMID 34112235, PMC8194016), 143 unrelated patients with common lymphatic malformation, combined lymphatic malformation or a syndrome, screened by targeted next-generation sequencing or digital droplet PCR: 'We identified a somatic PIK3CA mutation in resected lesions of 108 out of 143 patients (75.5%).' 79,920 x 0.755 = 60,340 patients
column12: a ceiling, and the trial's other filters are not cut because no published share exists for them. It admits only symptomatic disease with at least one measurable lesion on central review, and only participants 'not considered as a candidate for or ... not willing to receive non-drug therapies including but not limited to sclerotherapy, embolization, and surgery', which is the real narrowing and is almost certainly the larger of the two. So the share reads high. It reads low on one axis: the paper's cohort includes the syndromic cases the trial excludes, and it found hotspot mutations more frequent in common and combined lymphatic malformations than in the syndromes, so the mutant share in the trial's own population is probably above 75.5%. Testing is also a gate in practice, since 0.54% variant allele frequencies in tissue need a deep assay

column11: a judgement at one in ten, and the weakest row in this file. It is not anchored on a measured reach because none exists: the Orphanet survey itself states there are 'no treatments approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for either macrocystic or microcystic lymphatic malformations', so there is no incumbent whose share can be read. The competitive case for it: alpelisib would be the first labelled drug in the disease, the prescriber is the same vascular-anomalies specialist who already writes Vijoice for PROS, the comparator is procedural (sclerotherapy, embolisation, surgery) rather than pharmacological, and the mechanism is already proven in the adjacent PIK3CA-driven disease. The case against, which is why the number is not higher: the eligible share above has not been cut for the procedural filter the trial applies, so the pool it sits on is already generous, and sirolimus is used off label in these patients today
column12: the direction it errs in: unknowable from anything measured, which is the honest answer. The only measurement the book holds on this product is Vijoice's own CMS Part D series, 29 claims in 2022, 125 in 2023 and 214 in 2024 over 42 beneficiaries (drug_demand, asset 62), and Medicare Part D is close to irrelevant in a mostly paediatric disease, so it is a floor on a channel and not a share of a population. A peak share is settled by years of sales, not by an event. Replace it with a solved figure if a published peak-sales forecast for alpelisib in lymphatic malformations appears

column12: THE ROW TO ARGUE WITH FOR THIS LAYER, AND IT ERRS HIGH. A 30-day fill is a days-supply unit, so tablet strength does not enter it, which is the reason the book prefers this route to a dosage-unit count. But it is measured on Medicare beneficiaries taking alpelisib for advanced breast cancer, where the median duration of treatment is short and progression ends it. The layer it is being used for is lymphatic malformations with a PIK3CA mutation, a congenital lifelong condition in a population NCT05948943 enrols from age 6, where nothing progresses and treatment is indefinite. Persistence there should be far better than 37% of a year, so this row will understate the treated stock and understate the layer. I did not replace it with a judgement, because the brief's method is to measure on the patients the price is measured on and no alpelisib persistence figure exists for the overgrowth population. The series is stable enough to show the measure is real: days covered ran 0.3126, 0.3230, 0.3264, 0.3326, 0.3744 over 2020 to 2024
